signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags USD outperformance at +0.502% across 9 pairs against NOK underperformance at −1.320% across 2 pairs, establishing a 1.823% bilateral spread that clears the critical threshold. Spot trades at 9.466, pushing through the SMA20 at 9.363 and SMA50 at 9.402 to test the SMA200 at 9.489 after printing a wide-range bullish session. While Norges Bank maintains policy at 4.50% versus the Fed at 4.00% creating an apparent 50bp rate disadvantage for the dollar, retail positioning shows a 100% net long extreme in USD/NOK that signals crowded one-way exposure. The bilateral momentum gap dominates cross-asset flows as oil weakness (-1.21% to $89.7) exacerbates krone underperformance. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK, supported by bilateral G10 theme strength while holding above the SMA50. Catalyst: Norges Bank Financial Stability Report at 07:30 UTC. Risk: A daily close below the SMA20 at 9.363 invalidates the bullish momentum setup.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention-Driven Bid
signals.text: Confirmed data reported by WSJ verifies Japan deployed a record $50 billion in coordinated market action to defend the yen, establishing direct policy capping above current spot. USD/JPY trades at 157.99, holding above the SMA20 at 157.96 and SMA50 at 157.30 but capped beneath the SMA200 at 158.56. Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% maintains a 275bp policy rate advantage for USD, reflected in SOFR 3.92% vs TONA 1.23% giving a +269bp carry cushion. However, the options market prices aggressive downside tail risk: 1M 25d risk reversals print at −1.97, reflecting heavy put skew alongside elevated implied volatility of 6.9% versus 4.7% realized, yielding a +2.1% volatility risk premium. With VIX at 25.6, this move represents official policy enforcement on top of an otherwise carry-supportive backdrop rather than a safe-haven flight. Trade bias: Neutral to defensive USD/JPY, capped by official intervention scale. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 invalidates the official intervention ceiling.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Extreme + Rate Disadvantage
signals.text: CFTC positioning shows EUR leveraged funds net short −104,030 contracts, sitting at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of −1.80, confirming heavily crowded institutional short exposure. Spot trades at 1.1177, pinned below its SMA20 at 1.1195, SMA50 at 1.1347, and SMA200 at 1.1550 within an established technical downtrend. Retail sentiment stands at 85% long, directly diverging from institutional positioning and creating acute capitulation vulnerability if downside resumes. Central bank rate policy provides no relief, as Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% maintains a 135bp carry spread in favor of the dollar, reinforced by SOFR 3.92% vs €STR 2.44% providing a +148bp CIP carry advantage. With US 5Y yields showing real-yield-led strength over the 20-day horizon (-33bp real vs -11bp breakeven of -44bp nominal), broader rate dynamics continue to penalize the euro. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, driven by persistent carry disadvantage and contrarian retail overhang. Catalyst: United States CPI at 13:30 UTC. Risk: A daily close above the SMA20 at 1.1195 eases downside momentum and triggers spec short-covering.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Technical Breakdown vs Carry Anchor
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6888, breaking below its technical support zone near 0.6905 and remaining extended below the SMA20 at 0.6991, SMA50 at 0.7047, and SMA200 at 0.7060 in an entrenched downtrend. RBA at 4.85% vs Fed at 4.00% provides an 85bp policy carry buffer in favor of the Aussie, mirrored in OIS where AONIA 4.85% vs SOFR 3.92% provides a 93bp carry advantage. Leveraged funds hold net long +43,532 contracts, but positioning growth has stalled with WoW delta at −395 and 4W delta at −5,379, failing to absorb ongoing spot liquidation. BEER fair value model shows spot deeply discounted at z = −3.84σ against model fair value of 0.6979, but technical distribution currently overrides model valuation. Options skew confirms the caution, with 1M 25d risk reversals printing at −1.41 in favor of AUD puts. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, honoring the trend breakdown below 0.6905 despite supportive carry. Catalyst: United States CPI at 13:30 UTC. Risk: A sustained daily close back above 0.6905 invalidates the technical breakdown.
